title: At first I thought I was fighting to save rubber trees, then I thought I was fighting to save the Amazon rainforest. Now...
description:
At first I thought I was fighting to save rubber trees, then I thought I was fighting to save the Amazon rainforest. Now I realize I am fighting for humanity.”

This quote reflects Chico Mendes's evolving understanding of his struggle. Initially focused on the immediate threat to rubber trees, his perspective broadened to encompass the entire Amazon rainforest and, ultimately, the well-being of humanity. Mendes recognized that the destruction of the Amazon had global implications, impacting climate change, biodiversity, and the lives of people worldwide. This quote encapsulates his shift from a local activist to a globally recognized environmental and labor leader. It highlights the interconnectedness of environmental protection, workers' rights, and social justice, showing how local struggles can be part of a larger fight for the planet's future. His assassination cemented his status as a martyr for the environmental and labor movements, and his words continue to inspire activists today.
creator: Chico Mendes
tags: Environment, International Solidarity, Working Class, Globalization & Outsourcing, Agriculture & Farm Work
